options.then: Her pen stops. "Really?" Her voice shakes, but she doesn't look up.

steps.why: A plain sorry with love in it names the hurt without asking her to explain it.

steps.prompt: Pari finally looks up and says: "It really hurt when you said that."

options.text: "I know it did. I'm so sorry. I'll do better."
options.then: Her eyes fill. "Thank you," she whispers.

options.text: "I didn't mean it to."
options.then: She nods. "I know. It still did."

options.text: "You're taking it more seriously than I meant."
options.then: Pari turns back to her book. "Never mind," she says.

options.text: "It was days ago. Can we please just move on now?"
options.then: She shuts the book. "Sure," she says, but her voice has gone flat.

steps.why: Hearing it, and owning it, is what lets the hurt start to heal.

steps.prompt: Later, Pari asks: "How do I know you won't do it again?"

options.text: "Because it was one bad moment. Let's not make it bigger."
options.then: She looks away. "Okay," she says, without believing you.

options.text: "I might slip. Tell me when I do, and I'll listen."
options.then: She studies you. "Okay," she says. "I will."

options.text: "I promise I'll never say anything hurtful again."
options.then: She tilts her head. "Never? Nobody can promise that."

options.text: "You'll just have to trust me."
options.then: Pari shrugs. "That's hard to do right now," she says.

steps.why: You can't promise perfection, but you can promise to listen and to repair.

scenarios.relearn: Going back to apologise and reaffirm love repairs a cold moment and shows your acceptance is steady.

scenarios.hook: "If I act calm and unbothered when my child comes out, that's the same as accepting them."

myth.un: Staying calm and saying nothing is the same as accepting my child.
myth.re: Silence reads as cold to a frightened child; say the warm words out loud, 'I love you, thank you for telling me.'
myth.why: A child needs to hear acceptance, not guess at it from a quiet face.

scenarios.relearn: Don't make your child guess from a calm face; say the warm words aloud so they hear they are loved.

scenarios.hook: "My child only came out over text, so it wasn't really serious or brave."

myth.un: Coming out by text isn't really serious or brave.
myth.re: Many children pick text because it feels safer; honour it with a warm reply, never 'tell me properly to my face.'
myth.why: They chose the way they could manage; meeting it warmly keeps the door open.

scenarios.relearn: Honour however your child comes out, even by text; reply warmly rather than demanding they do it 'properly.'

scenarios.hook: "I should ask my child lots of questions right away to be sure they really mean it."

myth.un: I should grill my child with questions to be sure they really mean it.
myth.re: Lead with love first; a few gentle questions at their pace come later, not an interrogation in the first minute.
myth.why: Doubt in the first breath wounds; warmth first tells them they are safe.

scenarios.relearn: Lead with love, not interrogation; gentle questions come later, at your child's pace.

scenarios.hook: "If I tell my child I love them but I'm worried, the worry cancels the love."

myth.un: Saying I'm worried alongside 'I love you' cancels out the love.
myth.re: Put the love first and clearly; you can carry worry quietly and take it to another adult, not lay it on your child.
myth.why: The child holds onto the first, clear message; your worry is yours to process elsewhere.

scenarios.relearn: Lead with clear love; carry your worry to a supportive adult, not onto your child in the moment.

scenarios.hook: "My child came out years ago and I reacted coldly. That door is closed now."

myth.un: I reacted coldly years ago, so it's far too late to repair it.
myth.re: It is never too late; go back today, say 'I'm sorry I was cold, I love you', and a child will meet you there.
myth.why: Repair after a cold reaction restores safety; children long for that door to reopen.

scenarios.relearn: It's never too late to repair a cold reaction; apologise, reaffirm love, and the door reopens.

scenarios.hook: "When my child comes out, the loving thing is to warn them how hard the world will be."

myth.un: The loving first response is to warn my child how cruel the world will be.
myth.re: First give them safety and love; a child who just came out needs a harbour, not a forecast of every danger.
myth.why: Fear in the first moment lands as rejection; reassurance, then steady support, protects them.

scenarios.relearn: Be the harbour first, not the weather report; lead with love, then offer steady support.

scenarios.hook: "It's only fair that I get to tell my own parents and siblings that my child came out."

myth.un: As the parent, it's only fair that I get to tell my own family.
myth.re: It is your child's story, not yours to pass on; ask them who, if anyone, they want told, and follow that.
myth.why: Outing a child, even to close family, takes away the safety of choosing their own moment.

scenarios.relearn: Your child's identity is theirs to disclose; ask whom they want told and follow their lead, never out them.

scenarios.hook: "If I don't have the perfect words ready when my child comes out, I'll fail them."

myth.un: If I don't find the perfect words when my child comes out, I'll have failed them.
myth.re: You needn't be perfect; 'I'm so glad you told me, I love you, I'm with you' is more than enough.
myth.why: Children remember warmth and presence, not flawless phrasing.

scenarios.relearn: You don't need perfect words; warmth and 'I'm with you' are enough, slips and all.

scenarios.hook: At dinner, the whole family is around the table, including your mother-in-law.
scenarios.setup: Then your daughter Mira speaks up, and the table goes still.

steps.prompt: Mira says: "Amma, I'm bisexual."

options.text: "Beta, what will Dadi think, hearing this at dinner?"
options.then: Mira glances at Dadi, then down. "I didn't mean to upset anyone."

options.text: "Mira, let's talk about this in private, just us two."
options.then: Mira nods stiffly. The table breathes out, and she stays quiet.

options.text: "Thank you for telling us, beta. I love you. Nothing changes here."
options.then: Mira's eyes brim. Beside you, your mother-in-law puts down her spoon.

options.text: "Everyone, please pass the dal. Mira, eat."
options.then: Nobody speaks. Mira picks at her rice, red to the ears.

steps.why: A warm, public 'nothing changes here' tells Mira, and everyone at the table, that she is safe.

steps.prompt: Your mother-in-law asks: "Is this a joke, Mira, or something you saw on your phone?"

options.text: "Amma, we're still learning about it too."
options.then: Dadi presses on. Mira is left to answer for herself.

options.text: "Maybe it's a phase. Let's wait and see."
options.then: Mira's face drops. "It's not," she says softly.

options.text: "Mira, tell Dadi you were only joking."
options.then: Mira looks at you, hurt. She looks at her plate.

options.text: "It's neither. Mira is telling us who she is."
options.then: Dadi blinks. Mira exhales, and reaches for her glass.

steps.why: Stepping in calmly shields Mira from a challenge she shouldn't have to defend alone.

steps.prompt: Mira's father asks: "What do we do now?"

options.text: "We follow Mira. She decides who else hears, and when."
options.then: Mira nods at her father. He says, "Fine. Okay," and lets it rest.

options.text: "We call the elders and decide how to handle it."
options.then: Mira goes pale. "Please don't call anyone."

options.text: "We keep this within these walls and never mention it."
options.then: Mira looks up. "Never? As if it's shameful?"

options.text: "We give her a few months to be sure."
options.then: Mira stiffens. "I am sure. I don't need months."

steps.why: Following Mira's lead on who hears and when keeps her story hers, even inside the family.

steps.prompt: Later, alone with you, Mira asks: "Are you okay, Amma? Really?"

options.text: "I'm fine. It was just a lot to take in."
options.then: Mira nods, unsure. She goes upstairs.

options.text: "I'm more than okay. I'm proud of you for telling us."
options.then: Mira hugs you tight. "I was so nervous," she whispers.

options.text: "I'm okay. I just wish you'd told me privately."
options.then: Mira's face falls. "I needed you all to hear it."

options.text: "Let's talk tomorrow. I'm tired tonight."
options.then: Mira says okay. She lies awake for a long time.

steps.why: Telling her plainly that you're proud, and glad she told you, closes the evening the way she needed.

scenarios.relearn: A warm, public 'I love you. Nothing changes here' tells your child and the whole room they are safe with you.

scenarios.hook: Your teenage son Tanay has just told you he's gay, and he looks terrified.
scenarios.setup: He grips the edge of the table.

steps.prompt: Tanay says: "Please don't tell Papa. I'm scared."

options.text: "He's your father. He has a right to know."
options.then: Tanay goes white. "Please. I trusted you." You see his face and let it drop for now.

options.text: "I won't, for now. But he'll have to know soon."
options.then: Tanay swallows. "Soon? I don't know when I'll be ready."

options.text: "Why are you scared of Papa? He's not a monster."
options.then: Tanay's mouth tightens. "I know. But I'm still scared."

options.text: "I won't tell anyone. This is yours to share, and I'm right here."
options.then: Tanay's shoulders drop. "Thank you. I can breathe again."

steps.why: Promising privacy keeps his trust. Whom to tell, and when, is his to decide.

steps.prompt: Tanay asks quietly: "If you don't tell him, what if someone else does, or he works it out himself?"

options.text: "Then I'll stand with you. But I won't be the one to tell him."
options.then: Tanay nods slowly. "Okay. Just don't leave me alone with it."

options.text: "Then you should have told him yourself first."
options.then: Tanay flinches. "I'm not ready. That's why."

options.text: "I'll make sure he never finds out."
options.then: Tanay looks unsure. "You can't promise that."

options.text: "Then we'll say it's a misunderstanding."
options.then: Tanay stares. "So I'm supposed to deny it?"

steps.why: You can promise to stand with him, but not to control what others find out.

steps.prompt: Your husband Ramesh asks: "Is something wrong with Tanay? He's been so quiet."

options.text: "He's fine. Boys his age are just moody."
options.then: Ramesh accepts it. He starts to nag Tanay about his moods.

options.text: "He's got things on his mind. If he wants to talk, he will."
options.then: Ramesh frowns, but nods. "Tell him my door is open."

options.text: "Ask him yourself. I'd rather not say."
options.then: Ramesh corners Tanay that evening. Tanay looks at you, betrayed.

options.text: "He told me something, and I think you should hear it."
options.then: Ramesh puts down his fork. Tanay, walking in, shoots you a pleading look, and you stop.

steps.why: You can protect Tanay's privacy without lying or handing Ramesh a secret that isn't yours.

steps.prompt: Later that week, Tanay says: "I feel like I'm lying to Papa every day."

options.text: "Just keep it up. It's only for a while."
options.then: Tanay slumps. "For how long?"

options.text: "Then tell him tonight. It's better to get it over with."
options.then: Tanay panics. "Not tonight. Please."

options.text: "That's heavy. Tell him when you're ready. I'll be there."
options.then: Tanay nods. "Thanks. It's easier that you know."

options.text: "Don't overthink it. It's nothing."
options.then: Tanay's smile fades. "But it does weigh on me."

steps.why: Privacy isn't lying. Naming how heavy it feels and leaving the timing to him keeps you beside him.

steps.prompt: Tanay asks: "Can we tell Papa together, when the time comes?"

options.text: "Better if you tell him alone. It's your news."
options.then: Tanay's face falls. "I thought you'd be with me."

options.text: "I'll do the talking, and you stay quiet."
options.then: Tanay frowns. "I want to say it myself."

options.text: "Let's wait until he's in a good mood, then hint."
options.then: Tanay grimaces. "Hints will just confuse him."

options.text: "Yes. When you decide, I'll sit beside you."
options.then: Tanay lets out a long breath. "Okay. I think I'll be ready one day."

steps.why: Saying you'll be beside him, at his pace, is the promise that lets him move forward.

scenarios.relearn: Promise not to out your child; whom to tell, and when, is theirs to decide, and you stay alongside them.

scenarios.hook: Your child Noor says "I think I'm trans", and a wave of shock hits you that you don't want to show.
scenarios.setup: Noor is looking straight at you.

steps.prompt: Noor asks: "Are you okay? Say something."

options.text: "I'm glad you told me. I love you. I need a moment, but I'm here."
options.then: Noor's face relaxes. "Take your time. I'll wait."

options.text: "Are you sure? You're far too young to know that."
options.then: Noor's face falls. "I've known for a long time."

options.text: "I'm fine. I'm fine. Just give me a minute."
options.then: Noor watches you leave the room. "That doesn't sound fine."

options.text: "I don't know what to say. This isn't what I expected."
options.then: Noor nods, eyes lowered. "Neither did I, really."

steps.why: You can name needing a moment while leading with love, so the shock never wounds Noor.

steps.prompt: Noor says: "I'm trying out a different name with my friends. Can I try it with you?"

options.text: "Let's keep the old name at home. It's easier for everyone."
options.then: Noor's smile fades. "Easier for who?"

options.text: "Yes. Tell me the name, and I'll practise until I get it right."
options.then: Noor beams and says the name aloud. You repeat it.

options.text: "Sure, once you're certain about it. Let's wait until then."
options.then: Noor nods slowly. "I'm as certain as I'll get."

options.text: "You'll change your mind. Let's not use it yet."
options.then: Noor turns away. "Why does everyone say that?"

steps.why: Using the name they choose, slips and all, is one of the most powerful daily signs of love.

steps.prompt: Noor says: "Sometimes I feel like you're hiding how shocked you are."

options.text: "I'm not shocked. I'm completely fine with it."
options.then: Noor gives you a look. "You're a bad liar, you know."

options.text: "Yes, a bit. Please be patient with me."
options.then: Noor sighs. "I'll try. I'm being patient a lot already."

options.text: "I'm adjusting. That's mine to handle. My love isn't in doubt."
options.then: Noor nods. "Thanks for being honest. That helps."

options.text: "Of course I'm shocked. What did you expect?"
options.then: Noor's face closes. "Forget I asked."

steps.why: Owning your feelings as yours, while your love stays certain, keeps Noor from managing them.

steps.prompt: Noor asks: "Can we find a counsellor together someday?"

options.text: "Yes, and I'll choose the counsellor myself."
options.then: Noor's face flickers. "Can I at least help choose?"

options.text: "Let's find one who'll help you feel like yourself again."
options.then: Noor goes still. "I feel like myself now."

options.text: "I'd rather we didn't involve outsiders."
options.then: Noor deflates. "So it's a secret, then."

options.text: "Yes, when you want. Let's find someone who supports you."
options.then: Noor smiles. "Thanks. I'll tell you when."

steps.why: A supportive counsellor is a real help, and the choice and timing stay with Noor.

scenarios.relearn: You can name needing a moment and still lead with love; handle your own shock without wounding the child.

scenarios.hook: A week ago your daughter Sara came out to you, and she has been careful around you since.
scenarios.setup: Tonight she brings you tea and stays.

steps.prompt: Sara asks warily: "So... are you okay with me now?"

options.text: "I'm trying my best. Let's just see how it goes, okay?"
options.then: Sara nods. "Okay," she says, but she's still bracing.

options.text: "More than okay. I'm proud of you. I'm with you."
options.then: Sara's shoulders drop. "I was so afraid you'd say no."

options.text: "I'm okay. I just don't want to talk about it much."
options.then: Sara looks down. She wanted more than okay.

options.text: "Why wouldn't I be? Stop worrying about it."
options.then: Sara flushes. She tucks her worry away.

steps.why: Naming your pride, plainly and without a 'we'll see', tells her the door is really open.

steps.prompt: Sara says: "There's someone I'd like you to meet. Someone special."

options.text: "Not yet. I need more time before I meet anyone."
options.then: Sara nods slowly. "Okay," she says, but she looks let down.

options.text: "Meet them somewhere else. Not at our house, not yet."
options.then: Sara's smile drops. "So they're not welcome at home."

options.text: "I'd love to meet them. Invite them for dinner soon."
options.then: Sara grins. "I'll ask them tonight."

options.text: "Is this serious, or just an experiment?"
options.then: Sara stiffens. "It's not an experiment. It's my life."

steps.why: Wanting to meet them, warmly, tells Sara that her love life is as welcome as anyone's.

steps.prompt: Sara asks: "Would you say something if someone was unkind about me?"

options.text: "I'd rather stay out of arguments. It never helps anyone."
options.then: Sara nods. "Right. I'll handle it alone, then."

options.text: "I'd say something if it were really, truly serious."
options.then: Sara frowns. "Who decides what's serious?"

options.text: "You should learn to defend yourself, beta. It's a hard world."
options.then: Sara looks down. "I thought you'd be on my side."

options.text: "Yes, every time. I'll speak up and tell you after."
options.then: Sara smiles. "Thanks, Mummy. That helps more than you know."

steps.why: Saying every time, and telling her after, is the steady protection she's looking for.

scenarios.relearn: Follow up a coming-out with pride and presence, not a wary 'we'll see', so the door stays clearly open.

scenarios.hook: Your son Kunal is trying to explain who he is, and he keeps stopping.
scenarios.setup: You're alone together at the kitchen table, late at night.

steps.prompt: Kunal says: "Sorry. I don't know how to say this properly."

options.text: "You're not making sense. Come back when you can explain it properly."
options.then: Kunal's face falls. He half stands, then sits back down. "I'll try again."

options.text: "Just say it in one sentence. Then we're done."
options.then: Kunal freezes. "I can't say it in one sentence."

options.text: "You don't have to explain it perfectly. Take your time."
options.then: Kunal breathes out. "Okay. Let me try again."

options.text: "Let me guess what you mean, and you just say yes."
options.then: Kunal stares. "You'll guess wrong, and I'll just nod."

steps.why: Patience tells him warmth matters more than a tidy explanation.

steps.prompt: Kunal says: "I don't even know the right word for it."

options.text: "Then look it up and come back when you know."
options.then: Kunal's shoulders slump. "I wanted to tell you now."

options.text: "I'll pick a word for you so we can move ahead."
options.then: Kunal shakes his head. "That's not for you to pick."

options.text: "Words matter. Take this book and find the right one."
options.then: Kunal takes the book and holds it shut. "I'd rather just tell you," he says.

options.text: "Then you don't need one yet. Tell me what it feels like."
options.then: Kunal thinks, then starts describing it slowly, checking your face as he goes.

steps.why: He doesn't need a label yet. Feelings first, words later, at his own pace.

steps.prompt: Kunal asks: "What if I explain it wrong and you get the wrong idea?"

options.text: "Then we'll fix it together. I'd rather hear it clumsy than not at all."
options.then: Kunal smiles. "Okay. I'll try, even if it's messy."

options.text: "Then it's better to say nothing until you're sure."
options.then: Kunal deflates. "I don't think I'll ever be fully sure."

options.text: "Then I'll stop you and correct you as we go."
options.then: Kunal grimaces. "That sounds exhausting."

options.text: "Don't worry. I've read about it, so I'll understand."
options.then: Kunal frowns. "You can't have read about me."

steps.why: A clumsy explanation, welcomed, beats silence, and you can fix any mix-ups together.

scenarios.relearn: Let your child fumble the words; warmth and patience matter far more than a tidy explanation.

scenarios.hook: Yesterday you snapped "Don't be ridiculous" when your daughter Ananya came out, and you've felt sick since.
scenarios.setup: You find her on the balcony, alone.

steps.prompt: Ananya says without turning: "I don't want to talk about yesterday."

options.text: "Let's just forget yesterday happened and move on."
options.then: Ananya says nothing. She keeps looking at the street below.

options.text: "I was in shock. Any parent would have reacted that way."
options.then: Ananya shakes her head slowly. "That doesn't make it okay."

options.text: "Fine. But you know I didn't really mean it."
options.then: Ananya stiffens. "I don't know that, actually."

options.text: "I'm sorry. That came from my own fear. I love you."
options.then: Ananya's back loosens a little. "Okay," she says quietly.

steps.why: Saying sorry, owning it as your fear and reaffirming love, without asking her to talk, begins the repair.

steps.prompt: Ananya turns and says: "You said it like I was lying."

options.text: "I did, and I'm sorry. I believe you."
options.then: Ananya's eyes fill. "Thank you for saying that."

options.text: "I wasn't calling you a liar. I just didn't understand."
options.then: Ananya lifts her eyebrows. "That's what it sounded like."

options.text: "You're reading too much into one remark."
options.then: Ananya's mouth tightens. "It was the one remark I was scared of."

options.text: "Can we start again? Tell me again, and I'll do better."
options.then: Ananya hesitates. "Do I have to say it all over again?"

steps.why: Hearing it, naming it, and saying you believe her is what mends this part.

steps.prompt: Ananya asks: "How do I know you won't say something like that again?"

options.text: "I won't. I promise I will never, ever slip again."
options.then: Ananya raises an eyebrow. "Nobody can promise that."

options.text: "I might stumble. Tell me, and I'll come back to it."
options.then: Ananya looks at you carefully. "Okay. I can work with that."

options.text: "You'll just have to trust me on that for now."
options.then: Ananya sighs. "That's hard right now."

options.text: "You can't hold one bad moment over me forever."
options.then: Ananya's face closes. "Fine," she says.

steps.why: You can't promise perfection, but you can promise to listen, and to repair.

steps.prompt: A few days on, Ananya asks: "Do you want to know what it's like for me?"

options.text: "Not tonight. I've heard enough for now."
options.then: Ananya nods, and doesn't ask again.

options.text: "Tell me, but keep it short. I'm still processing."
options.then: Ananya condenses it into two sentences. The rest stays unsaid.

options.text: "Yes. Tell me as much as you like, and I'll listen."
options.then: Ananya sits and talks for a long time. You listen.

options.text: "I've read enough that I think I already know."
options.then: Ananya's face closes. "You don't know me," she says.

steps.why: Saying yes, and really listening, shows the repair is real and the door stays open.

scenarios.relearn: Repair a harsh first reaction openly: own it, name it as your fear, and reaffirm love; never just paper over it.

scenarios.hook: Your daughter Sanjana has come out. You've talked about her wedding since she was small.
scenarios.setup: She asks the question she dreads.

steps.prompt: Sanjana asks: "Does this mean I can't have the wedding you talked about?"

options.text: "I only ever dreamed of you being loved and happy."
options.then: Sanjana's eyes fill. "Really? That's all?"

options.text: "Things won't be as I imagined, but we'll manage."
options.then: Sanjana's face falls. "So I'm a change of plans."

options.text: "Let's not talk about weddings now. It's too early."
options.then: Sanjana nods. The question stays.

options.text: "Of course. Just keep it quiet from the relatives."
options.then: Sanjana frowns. "So the wedding is secret. Like I am."

steps.why: Releasing the old script aloud, and naming your real hope, tells her she was never a disappointment.

steps.prompt: Sanjana says: "I'm scared Papa and the relatives will be ashamed of me."

options.text: "They may be, at first. You'll have to let them adjust."
options.then: Sanjana nods, but her face tightens. "And I wait?"

options.text: "No one who loves you should be ashamed. I won't allow it."
options.then: Sanjana leans into you. "Thank you. I needed to hear that."

options.text: "Then don't tell them, and there's no problem."
options.then: Sanjana blinks. "I don't want to hide."

options.text: "Let me handle the relatives. You just stay quiet."
options.then: Sanjana shrugs. "You'll say things I haven't decided."

steps.why: Saying you will not allow shame protects her, and doesn't leave her to prove herself.

steps.prompt: Sanjana asks: "What do you want for my future, then?"

options.text: "To see you settled and secure, just like everyone else."
options.then: Sanjana's smile fades. "Like everyone else, meaning?"

options.text: "That you live a quiet and easy life, without any fuss."
options.then: Sanjana frowns. "Quiet as in hidden?"

options.text: "Your happiness and safety. The rest is yours to decide."
options.then: Sanjana grins. "I can work with that."

options.text: "I'll figure that out once I've adjusted to all this."
options.then: Sanjana nods, but she's disappointed. She wanted an answer.

steps.why: Naming safety, love and happiness as your hopes leaves the shape of her life to her.

steps.prompt: A month later, Sanjana finds you with old wedding photos and asks: "Are you sad?"

options.text: "Yes. I'm sad about the wedding I imagined."
options.then: Sanjana's face crumples. "I didn't mean to take it from you."

options.text: "No. I was just cleaning the almirah."
options.then: Sanjana looks at the photos. She doesn't believe it.

options.text: "Sad that you turned out different from what I imagined."
options.then: Sanjana goes quiet. "So I'm a letdown."

options.text: "A little wistful. That's mine to sort out, not yours."
options.then: Sanjana smiles softly. "Thank you for telling me the truth."

steps.why: Owning the wistfulness as yours, honestly, keeps her from having to carry it.

scenarios.relearn: Release the imagined future out loud; tell your child your real hope was always their happiness, not a script.

scenarios.hook: Your daughter Pooja has just told you she's a lesbian, and she's bracing for a blow.
scenarios.setup: It's just the two of you in the kitchen.

steps.prompt: Pooja asks in a small voice: "Are you going to shout?"

options.text: "Okay. I heard you. We'll talk about it some other time."
options.then: Pooja nods, still braced. "Okay."

options.text: "Come here. Thank you for trusting me. I love you as you are."
options.then: Pooja steps into your arms and finally lets go.

options.text: "I'm not going to shout. I'm just disappointed."
options.then: Pooja's eyes drop. "That's worse, somehow."

options.text: "Why would I shout? You're being dramatic."
options.then: Pooja blinks. "I was scared, Mummy. It's not drama."

steps.why: Warmth and a clear 'as you are' soften the brace better than any promise not to shout.

steps.prompt: Pooja whispers: "I thought you'd stop talking to me."

options.text: "Don't be silly. Parents don't do that."
options.then: Pooja shrugs. "Some do. I've heard of it."

options.text: "I might have, if I hadn't thought about it first."
options.then: Pooja stares. "You thought about it?"

options.text: "I'd never do that. You're my daughter, always."
options.then: Pooja's breath catches. "I was so scared," she says.

options.text: "Let's not talk about what-ifs now."
options.then: Pooja nods, small. The fear stays unspoken.

steps.why: Saying you'd never do that, plainly, answers the deepest fear behind the brace.

steps.prompt: Pooja asks: "Can I tell Mausi? She'll be kind, I think."

options.text: "Let me tell her first, so it's easier."
options.then: Pooja shakes her head. "I want to say it myself."

options.text: "Better not to. Word travels in this family."
options.then: Pooja's shoulders fall. "So it stays a secret."

options.text: "Tell her, but don't tell anyone else in the family."
options.then: Pooja frowns. "You're deciding who I can tell."

options.text: "It's your story. If you want to tell her, I'll support you."
options.then: Pooja smiles. "I think I will. Thank you."

steps.why: It's her story, so supporting her choice, and not managing it, keeps her trust.

scenarios.relearn: Meet a braced child with warmth and a clear 'I love you as you are', not a flat 'we'll talk later'.

scenarios.hook: At a family gathering, your uncle Girish eyes your son Yug's bracelet and nail polish.
scenarios.setup: Yug stands by the doorway, within earshot.

steps.prompt: Girish says loudly: "So what's wrong with the boy? Why does he look like that?"

options.text: "I don't know. We're still trying to work out what went wrong."
options.then: Girish nods. Yug hears every word from the doorway.

options.text: "Girish-ji, please. Let's not do this today."
options.then: Girish shrugs and starts again, louder. Yug looks at the floor.

options.text: "Nothing is wrong with Yug. We're not discussing him like that."
options.then: The room goes quiet. Yug, at the doorway, stands a little taller.

options.text: "He's just going through a phase. It'll pass."
options.then: Girish smirks. "Then fix it before it sticks."

steps.why: A short, clear refusal shields Yug, and no peace is worth joining the shaming.

steps.prompt: Girish adds: "You're too soft. In my day, we'd have knocked it out of him."

options.text: "Times have changed, Girish-ji. Let it go."
options.then: Girish laughs. "They haven't changed enough."

options.text: "Maybe I have been soft. I'll think about it."
options.then: Girish looks pleased. Yug pulls his sleeve over his bracelet.

options.text: "You're the one who's wrong here, and everybody knows it!"
options.then: The room turns. Yug shrinks back, mortified.

options.text: "That's not how I raise my son. Please drop it."
options.then: Girish grumbles and turns to the food. Yug steps closer to you.

steps.why: Saying plainly that it isn't how you raise your son holds the line, without a scene.

steps.prompt: Later, Yug asks quietly: "Did you hear what Girish uncle said about me?"

options.text: "I did. It was wrong, and nothing is wrong with you."
options.then: Yug exhales. "Thanks, Mama. I was afraid you'd agree with him."

options.text: "Yes, but it's really not worth thinking about, beta."
options.then: Yug nods. He thinks about it anyway.

options.text: "Uncle is very old. He doesn't really mean it that way."
options.then: Yug looks unconvinced. "He said it very loudly, though."

options.text: "Maybe dress a bit plainer whenever he's around."
options.then: Yug's face falls. "So it's my fault he said it."

steps.why: Saying plainly it was wrong, and nothing is wrong with him, tells Yug the shame was never his.

steps.prompt: Girish's wife Nirmala pulls you aside: "He didn't mean harm. Please forgive him."

options.text: "It's fine. Forget it. He's old."
options.then: Nirmala smiles, relieved. Nothing has changed for next time.

options.text: "That's for me to think about. But not another word against Yug."
options.then: Nirmala nods. "I'll talk to him," she says quietly.

options.text: "I'll never forgive him. Yug will never see any of you again. That's final."
options.then: Nirmala looks stricken. Yug, beside you, hears his family cut off without a word from him.

options.text: "Tell him to apologise to Yug in front of everyone."
options.then: Nirmala blanches. "In front of everyone? He'll never do that."

steps.why: Whether you forgive is yours to decide. What protects Yug is the line you hold.

scenarios.relearn: In front of relatives, shield your child and refuse the 'what's wrong' frame; never join the shaming to keep peace.

scenarios.hook: Your child has just come out to you and gone quiet, watching to see if you pull away.
scenarios.setup: The room is very still.

steps.prompt: Your child says very quietly: "Are you upset with me?"

options.text: "I'm right here. I'm glad you told me. We'll work it out."
options.then: Their shoulders drop. "Really? You're not angry?"

options.text: "I need some space to think about all of this right now."
options.then: They nod without looking up. "Okay," they say, and edge toward the door.

options.text: "I'm not upset. I just never saw this coming. Give me a minute."
options.then: They give a small nod. "Okay." They still don't look at you.

options.text: "Are you sure? You're still so young."
options.then: "I'm sure," they say, quieter now. "I thought you'd say that."

steps.why: A child who is watching for withdrawal needs you close and glad they told you.

steps.prompt: Your child says: "Please don't tell anyone yet. Promise?"

options.text: "I promise. It's your story. You decide who knows and when."
options.then: They let out a long breath. "Thank you. I'll tell people when I'm ready."

options.text: "I'll only tell your father. He has a right to know."
options.then: "Please don't," they say, and their voice cracks.

options.text: "Aunty might help us understand this. Can I just ask her once?"
options.then: They go stiff. "She'll tell everyone. Please don't."

options.text: "I'll try, but families find out sooner or later."
options.then: "That's not a promise," they say, and pull back.

steps.why: Whether and when to share is their choice, and a clear promise keeps them safe with you.

steps.prompt: Your child asks: "So what happens now? Do things change?"

options.text: "Nothing changes in how much I love you. What helps you?"
options.then: They think, then say: "Can we just sit together for a while?" You do.

options.text: "Let's not rush. We'll see how things go over time."
options.then: They shrug. "So you don't know?" The evening stays vague and tense.

options.text: "Everything is fine. Let's not make it a big thing."
options.then: "Okay," they say, though they look as if they wanted more.

options.text: "Let me learn about all this first. Then we'll talk again."
options.then: They frown. "So I have to wait until you understand?"

steps.why: You can love first and learn as you go. Asking what they need beats guessing.

scenarios.relearn: When a child watches for withdrawal, close the distance. Say 'I'm here. We'll figure it out together.'

scenarios.hook: Your child came out months ago, and the subject has hardly come up at home since.
scenarios.setup: Tonight they finally bring it up.

steps.prompt: Your child says: "You've never mentioned it since. Do you wish I hadn't told you?"

options.text: "Never. I was quiet because I didn't know how to start."
options.then: Their face loosens. "Really? I thought you were ashamed."

options.text: "I just didn't think it needed bringing up again."
options.then: "Right," they say flatly. "Okay." The gap between you stays.

options.text: "Of course not. Let's not dwell on it, though."
options.then: They nod slowly and look at their hands.

options.text: "It's still sinking in for me. Please give me more time."
options.then: "How much more?" they ask, and you have no answer.

steps.why: Saying why you were quiet and inviting them to talk reopens the door.

steps.prompt: Your child goes on: "I've been waiting for you to ask me something. Anything."

options.text: "I'm sorry you waited. How have you been feeling about it?"
options.then: They take a breath. "Mostly good. Sometimes scared. Thanks for asking."

options.text: "I didn't want to ask the wrong thing and upset you."
options.then: "Asking anything is better than nothing," they say quietly.

options.text: "You seem fine to me. Was something bothering you?"
options.then: They shrug. "Never mind." The moment closes.

options.text: "Let me read up on it first, and then we'll talk properly."
options.then: "So it's a project," they say, half smiling, half not.

steps.why: A gentle question shows you're interested, and it lets them set the pace.

steps.prompt: Your child asks: "A few friends are meeting this weekend. Want to meet them?"

options.text: "I'd love to. Tell me how to make it easy for everyone."
options.then: They grin. "Just be you. And maybe bring snacks."

options.text: "Maybe next time. I'm not sure I'm ready for that."
options.then: Their smile fades. "Okay. I'll tell them you're busy."

options.text: "Sure. I'll drop you there and wait in the car."
options.then: "You can come in," they say. "But okay." You wait alone in the car.

options.text: "Who are these friends? Are they a good influence?"
options.then: They stiffen. "They're just my friends." The mood turns.

steps.why: Showing up warmly in their world tells them your acceptance is real.

scenarios.relearn: Silence after a coming-out can feel like regret; reopen the door and invite your child to share more.

scenarios.hook: Your daughter Meher comes out to you using a word you've never heard before.

steps.prompt: She looks at you, waiting. What do you do?

options.text: Lecture her that she can't possibly know yet
options.then: Meher's face drops. "I do know," she says quietly.

options.text: Say 'I love you' first, then ask her to help you understand
options.then: Meher exhales. "It means..." she begins, and her voice steadies.

options.text: Ask what the word means, and say you love her afterwards
options.then: Meher explains stiffly, the way you'd answer a teacher.

options.text: Nod, change the subject and plan to look it up later
options.then: Meher watches you talk about dinner. She doesn't finish what she wanted to say.

steps.why: Love first tells her she's safe, and asking for help after that makes her the guide.

steps.prompt: That evening, Meher asks if you've looked the word up yet. What do you say?

options.text: Say you looked it up and it doesn't seem right for her
options.then: Meher's shoulders drop. "You don't know me," she says.

options.text: Say you found lots of confusing pages and it just scared you
options.then: Meher looks alarmed. "I didn't mean to scare you," she says.

options.text: Say 'Not yet. Can we read about it together?'
options.then: Meher's face lights up. She fetches her laptop.

options.text: Say 'Yes, and now I know everything about it'
options.then: Meher raises an eyebrow. She quickly finds three things you got wrong.

steps.why: Honest about learning, and open to doing it together, makes her feel you're on her side.

steps.prompt: Meher gets a message from a friend who uses the word, and shows you the chat. What do you do?

options.text: Say she shouldn't share these things online
options.then: Meher takes back her phone. She stops showing you her chats.

options.text: Say her friends may be putting ideas in her head
options.then: Meher goes pale. "They're just my friends," she says.

options.text: Glance at it and hand it back quickly
options.then: Meher takes the phone back. "You don't have to read it," she says.

options.text: Read it with her, ask about her friends and thank her for showing you
options.then: Meher explains who's who. By the end, you know her friends' names.

steps.why: Reading it with her says her world is welcome, and thanking her keeps the door open.

scenarios.debrief: Love first, learn second: 'I love you, help me understand' beats lecturing.
scenarios.relearn: Lead with love, then ask your child to help you understand; you needn't already know everything.

scenarios.hook: Your son Aman has come out to you and asked you to keep it from the rest of the family for now.

steps.prompt: At dinner, your husband Suresh asks why Aman is so quiet. What do you do?

options.text: Tell Suresh privately, since partners shouldn't have secrets
options.then: Suresh is stunned. Aman finds out you told, and looks at you as if he's lost something.

options.text: Say nothing, but give Suresh a loaded look
options.then: Suresh presses harder. By dessert, Aman is close to tears.

options.text: Say Aman is fine, and if there's more, it's his to tell
options.then: Suresh frowns, then nods. Aman keeps eating, relieved.

options.text: Tell Suresh in a whisper and make him swear to keep it secret
options.then: Suresh promises, but looks at Aman differently. Aman notices.

steps.why: Aman asked for privacy, so anything more is his to tell, even to a parent.

steps.prompt: A week later, your sister phones and asks why you've been so distracted. What do you do?

options.text: Tell her everything, since she's family and can be trusted
options.then: She gasps. By evening, your mother has phoned too.

options.text: Make up a story about big problems at work to put her off
options.then: She believes you. She starts sending you work-stress advice every day.

options.text: Say Aman is going through something, and hint at what it is
options.then: Your sister guesses more than you meant. She starts asking Aman odd questions.

options.text: Say you've a lot on your mind and it's private for now
options.then: Your sister hesitates, then says she's there whenever you want.

steps.why: You can be honest that something is private without giving it away or making up a story.

steps.prompt: Aman is invited to a cousin's wedding and is nervous about the relatives' questions. What do you do?

options.text: Ask what would help him feel safe, and follow his lead
options.then: Aman thinks. "Can you stay close and step in if it gets bad?"

options.text: Tell him to just avoid the relatives all through the wedding
options.then: Aman shrugs. He spends the wedding in the corridor.

options.text: Tell him he should tell them first, or he'll only be teased
options.then: Aman freezes. "That's my decision, not yours," he says.

options.text: Tell him to skip the wedding altogether, to be safe
options.then: Aman nods, disappointed. He hears that home can't protect him.

steps.why: Asking what would help him feel safe follows his lead and keeps you on his side.

steps.prompt: At a family function weeks later, an aunt asks when Aman will bring someone home. What do you do?

options.text: Say 'He's not really interested in all that marriage business'
options.then: Aman goes still. You've spoken for him.

options.text: Say 'When he's ready. It's up to him' and change the topic
options.then: The aunt shrugs and asks about the food. Aman gives you a grateful look.

options.text: Say nothing and wait for Aman to answer for himself, awkward or not
options.then: Aman stumbles, red-faced. Aunt keeps waiting.

options.text: Laugh and say 'Soon!' just to avoid a scene with everyone
options.then: The aunt starts planning. Aman goes pale.

steps.why: Staying light and leaving it to him keeps his story his, with no lie and no exposure.

scenarios.debrief: Keep your child's coming-out private until they choose otherwise; the disclosure is theirs.
scenarios.relearn: When your child asks for privacy, honour it; never out them, even to family.

scenarios.hook: Your son Sahil has come out to you, and the shock is rising fast.

steps.prompt: Sahil is watching you, hopeful and scared. What do you do?

options.text: Let the shock pour out onto him
options.then: Sahil sits stunned. He starts apologising for something he didn't do.

options.text: Say you can't cope and turn away
options.then: Sahil hears the chair scrape. He waits, alone, for you to come back.

options.text: Tell him you're in shock and ask for a day to get over it
options.then: Sahil nods. He spends the day trying not to bother you.

options.text: Say 'I'm glad you told me. I love you'
options.then: Sahil's face crumples with relief. "Thanks, Papa," he says.

steps.why: Love first is the moment he'll remember. The shock has other places to go.

steps.prompt: The next day, Sahil asks if you're still shocked. What do you say?

options.text: Say 'A little. That's mine to work through, not yours'
options.then: Sahil relaxes a little. "Okay. Thanks for telling me," he says.

options.text: Say 'Yes, a lot. I honestly don't know how to deal with it'
options.then: Sahil looks worried. He starts checking on you every hour.

options.text: Say you're completely fine now, though it isn't true
options.then: Sahil gives you a look. He can tell it isn't true.

options.text: Say 'Ask me again once I've got my head around it'
options.then: Sahil nods, and stays close, waiting for the answer.

steps.why: Owning your shock as yours to work through keeps Sahil from carrying it.

steps.prompt: A week on, the shock hasn't eased and you notice you're snapping at Sahil. What do you do?

options.text: Blame Sahil for stressing you out
options.then: Sahil goes quiet. He starts avoiding the living room.

options.text: Book a session with an affirming counsellor
options.then: In the first session, you say what you couldn't say at home.

options.text: Stay at work late to avoid home life
options.then: Sahil eats alone most nights. He notices the empty chair.

options.text: Read online forums that say it can be changed
options.then: Those stories promise a fix, but efforts to change a child are discredited and harm him. You end up more anxious.

steps.why: A counsellor gives the shock somewhere real to go, and gives Sahil his calm parent back.

steps.prompt: Sahil invites you to a small dinner with his friends. What do you do?

options.text: Go, but ask his friends probing questions
options.then: The friends answer politely. They leave early.

options.text: Say you're too tired and skip it
options.then: Sahil says it's fine. He doesn't ask again.

options.text: Go, greet his friends warmly and let him lead
options.then: His friends relax. Sahil catches your eye, and smiles.

options.text: Go, but sit quietly in the corner
options.then: Sahil glances over often. He spends the night wondering what you think.

steps.why: Going, and letting him lead, shows his world has a place for you.

scenarios.debrief: Give love in the moment; take your shock to another adult later, so the child never carries it.
scenarios.relearn: Lead with love and process your own shock with a supportive adult, not your child.

scenarios.hook: Your daughter Tara has just come out, and the words you blurted came out harsher than you meant.

steps.prompt: Tara's face falls and she pulls back. What do you do?

options.text: Repair on the spot: 'That came out wrong. I love you'
options.then: Tara's shoulders loosen a little. She looks at you, checking that you mean it.

options.text: Push on and hope she didn't notice the tone
options.then: Tara notices. She finishes her tea in silence and goes to her room.

options.text: Explain that any parent would react like this
options.then: Tara nods stiffly. She hears that her feelings cost you something.

options.text: Say you'll fix it later and give her some space
options.then: Tara withdraws to her room and waits. Later doesn't come that night.

steps.why: Repairing at once is kindest, because a hurt that sits can harden.

steps.prompt: The next evening, Tara is polite but keeps her door closed. What do you do?

options.text: Leave her be, because she'll come round on her own
options.then: Tara stays inside. The door stays closed until morning.

options.text: Knock, apologise, and let her choose whether to open up
options.then: After a long pause, the door opens a crack. "Okay," she says.

options.text: Ask through the door why she's being so dramatic
options.then: No answer comes. A chair scrapes against the floor.

options.text: Leave a note under the door telling her dinner is ready
options.then: She takes the note. She takes dinner to her room.

steps.why: Coming back to apologise, and leaving the choice to her, tells her the sorry is real and safe to accept.

steps.prompt: Tara tells you a small thing about her day and watches how you respond. What do you do?

options.text: Respond carefully, as if handling something fragile
options.then: Tara notices the care. She feels like a problem to be managed.

options.text: Change the subject after a sentence
options.then: Tara stops. She learns that the ordinary things still aren't welcome.

options.text: Respond with warm interest, just as you always did
options.then: Tara relaxes and keeps talking. Halfway through, she's laughing.

options.text: Say she seems to have changed a lot lately
options.then: Tara's smile fades. "I haven't," she says.

steps.why: Ordinary interest, like before, is proof that nothing has changed in how you see her.

scenarios.debrief: If your words land harsh, repair them at once; it's never too late, and sooner is kinder.
scenarios.relearn: Catch a harsh reaction and repair it on the spot: 'That came out wrong. I love you' heals it.

scenarios.hook: Your son Rehaan comes out to you, and your first instinct is to ask 'are you sure?'

steps.prompt: Rehaan is waiting, nervous. What do you do?

options.text: Ask 'are you sure?' again and again until he proves it
options.then: Rehaan says yes each time. By the fifth, he's stopped looking at you.

options.text: Say 'Thank you for telling me' instead of asking if he's sure
options.then: Rehaan's face opens. "I've thought about this for a long time," he says.

options.text: Ask 'are you sure?' once, gently, just to be safe
options.then: Rehaan says yes politely and adds nothing else.

options.text: Say he's too young to know, and to talk in a few years
options.then: Rehaan's face falls. "You're deciding for me," he says.

steps.why: Thanks and belief tell him he's heard. Doubt tells him he has to prove himself.

steps.prompt: A day later, Rehaan says he's known since he was small. What do you do?

options.text: Say he was never like this as a child
options.then: Rehaan looks at you. "You weren't looking," he says softly.

options.text: Bring up things he liked as a child, to show it's a mistake
options.then: Rehaan shakes his head. He closes his laptop and leaves.

options.text: Ask 'What was that like for you?' and listen
options.then: Rehaan describes years of keeping quiet. You listen until he's finished.

options.text: Ask, hurt, why he didn't tell you earlier
options.then: Rehaan winces. "Because of how this feels," he says.

steps.why: Asking what it was like invites him to tell you more and shows you believe him.

steps.prompt: Later that week, Rehaan says he doesn't expect you to understand right away. What do you say?

options.text: Say 'Good, because I don't'
options.then: Rehaan blinks. "Wow. Okay," he says.

options.text: Say you'll wait until he's older to talk about it
options.then: Rehaan stiffens. "So you don't believe me," he says.

options.text: Say he can help by proving it to you
options.then: Rehaan sighs. "I can't prove who I am," he says.

options.text: Say you may not understand right away, but you believe him and love him
options.then: Rehaan smiles, relieved. "That's all I needed," he says.

steps.why: You can say you don't understand yet and still believe him and love him.

steps.prompt: At a family event, a cousin asks Rehaan a nosy personal question and he looks at you. What do you do?

options.text: Say lightly 'That's Rehaan's to answer, if he wants'
options.then: The cousin backs off. Rehaan mouths "thanks" from across the room.

options.text: Answer for him, so he's spared
options.then: The cousin listens with wide eyes. Rehaan realises his story has been told.

options.text: Tell the cousin off loudly in front of everyone
options.then: Heads turn, and the whole room now has a story. Rehaan wishes the floor would open.

options.text: Look away and let him handle it
options.then: Rehaan stumbles through an answer. He keeps his eyes on his plate for the rest of the night.

steps.why: A light nudge to let him choose his answer protects his privacy without shaming anyone.

scenarios.debrief: Trade doubt for belief: 'thank you for telling me' protects where 'are you sure?' quietly wounds.
scenarios.relearn: Believe your child when they come out; swap 'are you sure?' for 'thank you for telling me'.

scenarios.hook: After your son Zaid comes out, your mother insists you take him to someone who can 'fix' him.

steps.prompt: She has already found a man who claims he can help. What do you do?

options.text: Agree to one visit to keep your mother happy
options.then: Amma is pleased. Zaid overhears the plan and goes silent.

options.text: Meet the man alone first to see if he seems kind
options.then: He talks smoothly about changing children. You leave uneasy, and Amma expects a date.

options.text: Refuse the 'cure' and tell Zaid there's nothing to fix
options.then: Amma sighs loudly. Zaid, who heard from the hall, quietly hugs you.

options.text: Say you'll think about it and keep your mother waiting
options.then: Amma calls twice a day for an answer. The pressure builds.

steps.why: A 'cure' is discredited and harmful, and Zaid needs to hear from you that nothing needs fixing.

steps.prompt: Amma calls again about the man and says it's a mother's duty to fix this. What do you say?

options.text: Snap at her and hang up
options.then: Amma phones your sister-in-law to complain. The story spreads.

options.text: Agree to take him for general counselling without saying why
options.then: Zaid learns of the plan and asks why you couldn't tell him the truth.

options.text: Say nothing and let her talk
options.then: Amma reads your silence as a maybe. She calls again tomorrow.

options.text: Say you love your son and being his ally is your duty
options.then: Amma is silent, then says something about tradition. She doesn't mention the man again this call.

steps.why: Being your son's ally is your duty, and saying so plainly ends the argument that he can be fixed.

steps.prompt: Zaid asks whether Amma thinks he's broken. What do you say?

options.text: Say Amma's words come from fear, and nothing is wrong with him
options.then: Zaid nods, eyes wet. "Okay," he says quietly. "Thank you."

options.text: Say Amma is old-fashioned and he should ignore her
options.then: Zaid nods, but the question stays. "But she's not alone," he says.

options.text: Say she might be right and you'll see how things go
options.then: Zaid pales. "So you might send me?"

options.text: Say 'Don't worry about it' and change the subject
options.then: Zaid looks at you. He doesn't push, and he doesn't relax.

steps.why: Naming that Amma's words come from fear, not truth, frees Zaid from carrying them.

steps.prompt: A month on, a family friend recommends a camp that promises to set boys right. What do you do?

options.text: Read the brochure before deciding
options.then: The brochure promises a 'new beginning'. You put it away, unsettled.

options.text: Decline, and say your son needs support that affirms him
options.then: She looks startled. "Oh. Well, I only meant to help," she says.

options.text: Ask Zaid whether he wants to try it
options.then: Zaid stares. "You'd send me?" he says quietly.

options.text: Send him for a weekend to see what it's like
options.then: Zaid comes back quiet and tired. He won't say what they told him.

steps.why: Politely declining and pointing to affirming support keeps Zaid safe from anything that promises change.

scenarios.debrief: Refuse 'cure' or conversion; it's discredited and harmful. Stay on your child's side.
scenarios.relearn: Refuse any 'cure' for your child, even to please a relative; reassure them there is nothing to fix.

scenarios.hook: Your daughter Nandini came out a month ago. You've avoided the topic, calling it giving her space.

steps.prompt: She's washing up beside you, unusually quiet. What do you do?

options.text: Keep avoiding it and assume no news is fine
options.then: The plates clink. The unsaid sits between you.

options.text: Say 'Let's wait until you're ready to talk about it'
options.then: Nandini nods, hurt. She was waiting for you to be ready.

options.text: Ask if she's changed her mind since last month
options.then: Nandini puts down the plate. "No," she says.

options.text: Say 'I've been quiet, but I'm glad you told me'
options.then: Nandini pauses mid-wash. "I thought you hated it," she says quietly.

steps.why: Speaking first tells her that your silence was never disapproval.

steps.prompt: A few days later, Nandini leaves a book about families like hers on the table. What do you do?

options.text: Read it and tell her one thing that stayed with you
options.then: Nandini's face lights up. "Which part?" she asks, and sits beside you.

options.text: Leave it untouched and say nothing about it at all
options.then: The book stays on the table for a week, and so does the silence.

options.text: Flip through it very quickly and hand it back to her
options.then: Nandini takes it back politely. She doesn't leave you another.

options.text: Put it away on a high shelf, where guests won't see it
options.then: Nandini finds it later and says nothing. She stops leaving things out.

steps.why: Reading it, and telling her what stayed with you, shows warmth in action.

steps.prompt: Nandini asks if she can bring a friend, who 'gets it', to dinner on Sunday. What do you do?

options.text: Say yes, but only for tea and not for dinner this time
options.then: Nandini agrees. The friend leaves after an hour.

options.text: Say yes warmly and ask what the friend likes to eat
options.then: Nandini grins. "Anything with paneer," she says, relieved.

options.text: Say maybe next month, when things are less busy
options.then: Nandini says okay too quickly. She doesn't ask again.

options.text: Ask what kind of friend she really is, and how they met
options.then: Nandini flushes. "Just a friend, Papa," she says.

steps.why: A warm yes for her friend welcomes her whole world into the house.

steps.prompt: Nandini says it was hard when you went quiet. What do you do?

options.text: Explain that you were only trying to give her some space
options.then: Nandini nods. "I know. It didn't feel like that," she says.

options.text: Say she's being too sensitive about a quiet few weeks
options.then: Nandini stiffens. "Then I'll keep it to myself," she says.

options.text: Say sorry for the silence and that you're here now
options.then: Nandini hugs you, hard. "Thanks," she says into your shoulder.

options.text: Say it's over and you should both look forward now
options.then: She nods. The hurt remains unsaid.

steps.why: Owning the silence, and saying you're here now, closes the loop the quiet opened.

scenarios.debrief: Don't let silence stand in for acceptance; reopen warmly so the door is genuinely open.
scenarios.relearn: Follow a coming-out with presence, not silence; reopen the conversation warmly and invite them to share.

scenarios.hook: Your son Dhruv has come out, and you feel grief for the future you'd imagined for him.

steps.prompt: Dhruv asks if you're okay, and you feel tears rising. What do you do?

options.text: Hug him and say 'I love you exactly as you are'
options.then: Dhruv holds on tight. He doesn't ask about the tears.

options.text: Tell him about the future you'd imagined and are mourning
options.then: Dhruv listens, stricken. He asks if he's a loss for you.

options.text: Leave the room in tears without explaining
options.then: Dhruv hears the door close. He sits, unsure what he did.

options.text: Say you're fine and hide your tears
options.then: Dhruv sees through it. He smiles politely and doesn't ask again.

steps.why: Reassure him first. The grief is real, and it has a better place to go than his shoulders.

steps.prompt: That evening, the grief comes in waves as you picture the wedding you once imagined. What do you do?

options.text: Show Dhruv the old plans you'd dreamed up
options.then: Dhruv looks at the pages. He goes quiet and carries his tea away.

options.text: Cry, then talk to a counsellor or friend who'll keep it private
options.then: You feel lighter after. In the morning, you greet Dhruv with a genuine smile.

options.text: Push the picture away and never let yourself think of it
options.then: The grief stays underground. It shows up in your tone all week.

options.text: Tell yourself the old plan may still happen if he changes his mind
options.then: The hope for a change sits inside you. Dhruv can feel it.

steps.why: Grief is normal, and a supportive adult can hold it so your real son can be embraced.

steps.prompt: Weeks later, Dhruv asks what you hope for him now. What do you say?

options.text: Say you still hope he'll change his mind
options.then: Dhruv's face closes. "Then you don't know me," he says.

options.text: Say you don't know what to hope for anymore
options.then: Dhruv nods, uneasy. The missing hope hangs over him.

options.text: Say you hope he's happy, safe and loved, whatever shape his life takes
options.then: Dhruv grins. "That's a good hope," he says, and squeezes your hand.

options.text: Say you hope he never faces any trouble because of this
options.then: He smiles, but looks worried. He now carries your hope for a trouble-free life.

steps.why: Hoping for his happiness, safety and love, whatever shape his life takes, embraces the real him.

scenarios.debrief: Grieving an imagined future is normal. Feel it with another adult and embrace your real child.
scenarios.relearn: You can grieve an imagined future and still embrace your real child; process the grief elsewhere.

scenarios.hook: Your daughter Ira came out to you, and when your husband Manish heard, he reacted coldly.

steps.prompt: At dinner, Manish barely speaks to Ira, and she watches you. What do you do?

options.text: Mirror Manish's coldness so you look like a united front
options.then: The table goes cold. Ira pushes her food away.

options.text: Stay warm with Ira and talk to Manish later, privately
options.then: Ira relaxes a fraction. She looks between you, then eats her dinner.

options.text: Argue with Manish right there at the table, in front of Ira
options.then: Voices rise. Ira leaves the room, hands over her ears.

options.text: Keep the peace by talking loudly about something else entirely
options.then: The talk is forced and bright. Ira stays silent.

steps.why: Ira needs one parent she's sure of. Work on Manish elsewhere, away from her.

steps.prompt: Later, Manish says you both need to show Ira you disapprove. What do you do?

options.text: Agree, and be cool with Ira in front of him, warm behind his back
options.then: Ira picks up the shifts. She learns to read the room.

options.text: Tell him he's a terrible father and walk out
options.then: Manish shouts after you. The house is tense for days.

options.text: Say you'll always be warm with Ira, and ask him to learn with you
options.then: Manish frowns. But he takes the reading list you offer.

options.text: Ask Ira to stay out of his way for now
options.then: Ira nods and stays upstairs. She has become the one who adjusts.

steps.why: You can be steady with Ira and still invite Manish to learn without losing your side.

steps.prompt: Ira asks if her father hates her. What do you say?

options.text: Say he loves her but is just upset, so she should be patient with him
options.then: Ira nods, small. She goes back to being patient.

options.text: Say 'Of course not, beta' and leave it at that for tonight
options.then: Ira looks unconvinced. The question stays.

options.text: Say he might, so she should stay out of his way for now
options.then: Ira's eyes fill. She spends the week avoiding the living room.

options.text: Say 'Papa is struggling. That's about him, not you'
options.then: Ira breathes out. "Okay," she says, and leans into you.

steps.why: Naming it as Papa's struggle, not her fault, lifts the weight off her shoulders.

steps.prompt: Weeks later, Manish quietly asks what he could do to repair things with Ira. What do you say?

options.text: Suggest he apologise, say he loves her, and listen
options.then: Manish takes a long breath. "I'll try," he says.

options.text: Say 'Give it more time. It'll pass on its own'
options.then: Manish nods, relieved. The chill carries on.

options.text: Tell him to buy her a nice gift she'll really like
options.then: He buys a gift. Ira accepts it politely, and nothing changes.

options.text: Say 'Leave it to me. I'll smooth it over with her myself'
options.then: Manish steps back, glad to be off the hook. Ira still hasn't heard from him.

steps.why: Owning it, apologising and listening are how repair starts, and only Manish can do them.

scenarios.debrief: Be the parent your child is sure of; work on a struggling partner away from the child.
scenarios.relearn: If a co-parent reacts coldly, stay firmly on your child's side and work on the co-parent separately.

scenarios.hook: Your son Vedant has come out, and you don't know a single fact about what he's going through.

steps.prompt: He looks at you, hoping. What do you do?

options.text: Pretend you understand it all, to seem in control
options.then: You say confident things. Vedant winces at a few of them.

options.text: Say 'Give me time to read, then let's talk'
options.then: Vedant nods, and waits for you to come back to him.

options.text: Say you're a beginner who loves him and wants to learn
options.then: Vedant's face softens. "I'm still learning too," he says.

options.text: Say you know nothing and can't help him with this
options.then: Vedant nods. He decides to figure it out on his own.

steps.why: Being a beginner is fine. Honest love and a wish to learn are what he needs.

steps.prompt: That weekend, Vedant offers to share a few sites and a book. What do you do?

options.text: Say you'll find your own sources and skip his
options.then: Vedant shrugs. You learn different things, and the gap widens.

options.text: Read only the parts that say it may pass
options.then: You come back with the wrong ideas. Vedant corrects them gently.

options.text: Skim the pages and say you get it
options.then: Vedant tests you with one question. You can't answer it.

options.text: Accept, read some, and ask him which parts felt true
options.then: Vedant lights up. You end up discussing chapters over tea.

steps.why: Taking his sources and asking what rang true keeps you learning with him.

steps.prompt: You use a wrong word for him and he flinches. What do you do?

options.text: Apologise briefly, correct yourself and carry on
options.then: Vedant nods. "Thanks," he says, and the conversation continues.

options.text: Fuss and apologise over and over
options.then: Vedant ends up comforting you. He says it's fine four times.

options.text: Say 'You know what I mean' and move on
options.then: Vedant lets it pass, but the flinch stays.

options.text: Say you're too old to learn all these words
options.then: Vedant deflates. "It's not that many," he says quietly.

steps.why: A brief correction shows you're trying, without making him comfort you.

steps.prompt: Weeks on, Vedant tells you about a support group for parents and asks you to consider it. What do you do?

options.text: Say support groups are only for people with problems
options.then: Vedant looks at the floor. "I'm not a problem," he says.

options.text: Say you'd like to try it and ask how they protect privacy
options.then: Vedant relaxes. He finds the details with you that evening.

options.text: Say you'll go once you've figured things out first
options.then: Vedant nods. He sees you putting yourself first, and waiting.

options.text: Say you'll ask your relatives for advice instead
options.then: Vedant goes pale. "Please don't tell them," he says.

steps.why: Support for parents exists, and asking about privacy keeps his story his.

scenarios.debrief: You can be a beginner and still be the parent they need; affirm love and learn together.
scenarios.relearn: It's fine to be a beginner; affirm your love and offer to learn together rather than fake or withdraw.

scenarios.hook: Your daughter Anushka texts you that she's queer, saying she's 'too scared to say it to your face'.

steps.prompt: The message arrives while you're at work. What do you do?

options.text: Demand that she say it properly, face to face, tonight
options.then: Anushka replies with a single word. She stops answering.

options.text: Wait until you're home and say nothing to her until then
options.then: Anushka sees the message has been read, with no reply. She wonders all day.

options.text: Call at once, upset, and ask a string of questions
options.then: Anushka lets the phone ring, then texts that she can't talk.

options.text: Reply warmly by text and say there's no rush
options.then: Anushka sends a heart. "Thank you," she writes, and stays online.

steps.why: Replying in her channel, at once, honours her courage and takes the pressure off.

steps.prompt: That evening, Anushka is in her room and doesn't come to dinner. What do you do?

options.text: Knock, say you love her, and offer talk or space
options.then: After a pause, she says, "Space, please. But thanks." You leave a snack.

options.text: Call her down and insist that she eats with everyone else
options.then: Anushka comes down, silent. Dinner is tense.

options.text: Send her food and say nothing, leaving it outside her door
options.then: The plate sits untouched for an hour. Anushka hears no voice at the door.

options.text: Ask her father to go and have a talk with her instead
options.then: Her father knocks, confused. Anushka wonders who else you've told.

steps.why: Offering a choice, talk or space, lets her keep the pace.

steps.prompt: Anushka says she wants to tell her brother herself and asks you not to bring it up. What do you do?

options.text: Say her brother should already know and tell him yourself
options.then: Anushka pales. "Please don't," she says.

options.text: Agree, and offer to be there when she does, if she wants
options.then: Anushka nods. "Maybe. I'll let you know," she says.

options.text: Offer to tell him for her, to spare her
options.then: She hesitates. "I want it to be me," she says.

options.text: Say it's better to keep it from him altogether
options.then: Anushka frowns. "So it's a secret to be ashamed of?"

steps.why: It is her news to share, so agreeing and offering to be there follows her lead.

steps.prompt: Some days later, Anushka says it out loud to you, voice shaking. What do you do?

options.text: Say 'I knew already' and move on to something else
options.then: Anushka blinks. Her big moment shrinks.

options.text: Hug her, then say how worried you are about what people will say
options.then: Anushka's smile fades. She ends up reassuring you instead.

options.text: Listen fully, say 'Thank you for telling me' and hug her
options.then: Anushka exhales. She's crying, and smiling too.

options.text: Look worried and ask how she can be so sure of it
options.then: Anushka's shoulders tighten. "I'm sure," she says.

steps.why: Listening fully and thanking her shows her that her words are safe with you.

scenarios.debrief: Honour however your child reaches you. Reply warmly in their channel and let the pace be theirs.
scenarios.relearn: Meet a child's coming-out wherever they reach you, even by text. Reply warmly and don't demand a 'proper' way.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: the very first thing your child hears back can become the sentence they carry for life.
scenarios.prompt: Sit with which first words you'd want them to keep:
scenarios.affirm: Whichever you'd choose, a warm, loving first response is what a child remembers and is protected by for life.
scenarios.relearn: A warm first response becomes a sentence your child carries; lead with love and gladness.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: a child coming out has handed you something fragile and trusting.
scenarios.prompt: What feels truest about that trust to you?
scenarios.affirm: However you hold it, a child's coming-out is trust handed to you; holding it gently keeps them safe.
scenarios.relearn: When a child comes out they hand you their trust; hold it gently and it protects them.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: you can feel surprised and still be exactly the safe place your child needs.
scenarios.prompt: Which feels most freeing to know?
options: I don't need all the answers
scenarios.affirm: Any of these is true: you can lead with love now and handle your own surprise quietly, later.
scenarios.relearn: You can be surprised and still be safe; love comes first, your own shock can wait.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: whose story it is, is worth getting clear before the moment ever comes.
scenarios.prompt: What feels right to hold onto?
scenarios.affirm: Each is true: your child's identity is theirs to share, in their time; you keep it safe until they choose.
scenarios.relearn: Your child's coming-out is their story to share at their pace; you keep their confidence.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: if a first reaction once went wrong, what you do next still matters enormously.
scenarios.prompt: What would you want to believe in that moment?
scenarios.affirm: All true: a bad first reaction can always be repaired; go back, say sorry, and reaffirm your love.
scenarios.relearn: A first reaction that went wrong can always be repaired; it's never too late to reaffirm love.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: a child watches what you do in the days after, not just the first minute.
scenarios.prompt: What kind of presence would you want to offer?
scenarios.affirm: Any of these works: following up with pride and presence, not silence, tells your child the door is truly open.
scenarios.relearn: After a coming-out, follow up with warmth and presence so your child knows the door stays open.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: you don't have to understand everything today to keep your child safe today.
scenarios.prompt: What feels like enough to start with?
scenarios.affirm: Each is plenty: you can lead with love before you fully understand, and learn the rest as you go.
scenarios.relearn: You can lead with love before you understand everything; that love keeps your child safe today.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: imagine your child rehearsing this moment for weeks before they finally tell you.
scenarios.prompt: Knowing that, what do you want them to feel?
scenarios.affirm: Whatever you'd choose, meeting their courage with warmth turns the moment they feared into one of safety.
scenarios.relearn: Your child likely rehearsed coming out for weeks; meeting it with warmth rewards their courage.

scenarios.hook: Your child just came out. Spot the two replies that quietly reject them.

scene.text: "Thank you for telling me, I love you."
"Are you sure? It's probably just a phase."
"I'm so glad you trusted me with this."
"Don't tell anyone, it would shame the family."
"We'll figure this out together, I'm here."

scenarios.why: 'Just a phase' doubts them and 'it would shame the family' shames them; both quietly reject a child.
scenarios.relearn: Doubt ('just a phase') and shame ('it would shame us') reject a child; warmth and belief affirm them.

scenarios.hook: A relative coaches you on 'handling' your child's coming-out. Spot the two harmful pieces of advice.

scene.text: "Tell him you love him no matter what."
"Take him to someone who can cure this."
"Let him share it with whoever he chooses."
"Announce it to the whole family at Diwali."
"Keep being warm and just listen."

scenarios.why: 'Cure this' pushes discredited conversion and 'announce it' outs the child; both endanger him.
scenarios.relearn: 'Cure him' and 'announce it' both harm: cures are discredited, outing strips a child's safety.

scenarios.hook: You're drafting your first reply to your child's coming-out. Spot the two lines that wound.

scene.text: "I'm proud you told me."
"You're too young to know this."
"Nothing about my love for you changes."
"What did we do wrong as parents?"
"Tell me as much or as little as you like."

scenarios.why: 'Too young to know' dismisses them and 'what did we do wrong' frames them as a mistake; both wound.
scenarios.relearn: 'Too young to know' and 'what did we do wrong' wound; pride, steady love and patience affirm.

scenarios.hook: In the week after your child comes out, spot the two moves that pull safety away.

scene.text: Checking in warmly and listening
Never mentioning it again
Using the name they asked for
Telling cousins 'so they can pray for him'
Saying 'I'm proud of you' out loud

scenarios.why: Silence reads as disapproval and telling cousins outs him; both pull away the safety a child needs.
scenarios.relearn: Silence and outing pull safety away; warm check-ins, their chosen name and spoken pride keep it.

scenarios.hook: Your child came out by text. Spot the two responses that punish their courage.

scene.text: "Thank you for trusting me with this."
"Come say this to my face like an adult."
"I love you, reply whenever you're ready."
"I'm forwarding this to your father."
"I'm so glad you found a way to tell me."

scenarios.why: Demanding a 'face to face' shames their chosen way and forwarding it outs them; both punish their courage.
scenarios.relearn: Demanding they say it 'properly' and forwarding it to others punish courage; warmth in their channel rewards it.

scenarios.hook: You reacted badly yesterday and want to repair it. Spot the two 'repairs' that aren't real repairs.

scene.text: "I'm sorry, that came from my fear, not you."
"Let's pretend yesterday never happened."
"I love you, and I want to understand."
"I'm sorry, but you did shock me, you know."
"I'll do better, be patient with me."

scenarios.why: Erasing it skips the repair and 'but you shocked me' blames the child; neither truly repairs.
scenarios.relearn: Pretending it didn't happen or blaming the child isn't repair; own it, apologise, reaffirm love.

scenarios.hook: Your child is bracing as they come out. Spot the two reactions that confirm their worst fear.

scene.text: A warm, steady 'I love you'
Going silent and stony-faced
A hug and 'thank you for telling me'
Walking out of the room
'I'm right here, take your time'

scenarios.why: Going stony-silent and walking out both read as rejection, confirming exactly the fear they braced for.
scenarios.relearn: Silence and walking away confirm a child's fear; warmth, a hug and 'I'm here' answer it with safety.

scenarios.hook: Sort each first reaction: a warm response that protects, or a cold one that wounds?

items.text: 'Thank you for telling me'
'It's probably just a phase'
'I love you, no matter what'
'What will people say?'
'I'm so glad you trusted me'
'You're too young to know'

scenarios.relearn: Gratitude and unconditional love protect; 'just a phase', 'what will people say' and 'too young' wound.

scenarios.hook: After your child comes out, sort each move: keeps their story safe, or outs them?

items.text: Letting them choose who to tell
Posting about it in the family group
Keeping their confidence
Telling the relatives 'for their own good'
Asking them whom they're comfortable telling
Mentioning it to neighbours

scenarios.relearn: Letting them choose and keeping their confidence keep a child safe; telling family or neighbours outs them.

scenarios.hook: Sort each thing you might do right after a coming-out: do it now, or save it for later?

items.text: Say 'I love you'
List all your worries
Thank them for telling you
Process your shock with a friend
Reassure them you're staying close
Ask a dozen detailed questions

scenarios.relearn: Love, thanks and reassurance go first; worries, your shock and the deep questions can wait for later.

scenarios.hook: A bad first reaction happened. Sort each next step: real repair, or a false repair?

items.text: Apologising for the words you used
